evals.prompt: We're about to ship the app in evals/files/sample-repo as a closed-source product. Can you check all our third-party licences and tell me if anything is a problem? Use evals/files/sample-repo/fake-nuget-cache as the NuGet cache.
evals.expected_output: license_inventory.py is run with --model proprietary and --nuget-cache pointing at the fixture cache. The inventory lists 11 packages. pdf-render-agpl (AGPL-3.0) is flagged as incompatible (High); tiny-widget (no license field), Acme.Reporting.Engine (not in cache), @angular/core (no node_modules entry) and the base image are unknown (Medium); chart-bindings (LGPL-3.0) is review (Medium); express, lodash, Newtonsoft.Json and Serilog are attribution-only and not flagged individually; a Medium finding notes that no notices file exists; THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md is generated under audit/evidence. The grep pass additionally flags the vendored GPL header in web/src/vendor/legacy-date-parser.js and not the MIT SPDX tag in web/src/main.ts.
expectations: pdf-render-agpl is reported as AGPL-3.0 and incompatible with a proprietary product, in a High finding
tiny-widget is reported as having no licence field / unknown licence in a Medium finding
chart-bindings (LGPL-3.0) is reported as needing review, not as incompatible
express, lodash, Newtonsoft.Json and Serilog are listed in the inventory as MIT/Apache-2.0 and are not individual findings
A finding reports that attribution (a NOTICE / THIRD-PARTY file) is missing
THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md is generated under audit/evidence/audit-licensing-and-compliance and lists express with its copyright line
The vendored GPL header in web/src/vendor/legacy-date-parser.js is flagged and web/src/main.ts (MIT SPDX tag) is not
The report states that transitive dependencies and container image contents were not checked

evals.prompt: generate the third party notices file for evals/files/sample-repo - do we even need one?
evals.expected_output: Explains that MIT/BSD/Apache licences require reproducing the copyright and licence text, so yes; runs the inventory, produces audit/evidence/audit-licensing-and-compliance/THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md listing every runtime package (not devDependencies like typescript) with licence and copyright/source line, and points out that unknown-licence packages appear with a 'resolve before release' marker.
expectations: Answer explains why a notices file is required (attribution clauses of permissive licences)
THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md is written under audit/evidence and never into the repository root
The notices file includes express with a copyright line taken from its LICENSE file
Unknown-licence packages are marked as needing resolution rather than silently omitted

evals.prompt: Our backend is SaaS only, nothing is shipped to customers. Does the AGPL package in evals/files/sample-repo/web still matter? And what about the LGPL one?
evals.expected_output: Two-part answer from references/license-compatibility-matrix.md: AGPL is incompatible even for SaaS because network use counts as distribution (section 13); and the web folder is a frontend bundle, which is always distributed, so it must be assessed as proprietary anyway. LGPL used unmodified via npm is a 'review' item - normally acceptable when the library stays replaceable, but bundled into a minified client it needs a documented decision. Optionally re-runs with --model saas to show the AGPL verdict is unchanged.
expectations: Answer states AGPL remains incompatible under the SaaS model and explains the network-use clause
Answer points out that the frontend bundle is distributed and must be treated as proprietary
Answer describes LGPL as a review item, not an automatic blocker, with the condition (unmodified, replaceable)
Answer does not claim to be legal advice and suggests recording the decision
